stories.title: New AI tech considered to tackle wrong-way driving
stories.summary: AI technology could be used to help alert people more quickly to potential motorway incidents, according to Minister of State at the Department of Transport Seán Canney. He made the comments during a media briefing in which he also said new laws for people driving the wrong way down motorways will be drafted next week. In the wake of the fatal M9 motorway crash earlier this month, the Government is continuing to consider new plans to protect people from a repeat incident. The plans were discussed in more detail today by Mr Canney, who met with gardai, Transport Infrastructure Ireland and the Road Safety Authority.

stories.title: Forum recommends tackling energy costs for businesses
stories.summary: Energy has been identified as the principal contributor to rising business costs by an advisory forum established by the Government. The Cost of Business Advisory Forum has issued its final report setting out 63 recommendations to boost competitiveness and cut costs. The report found that the Government should consider the feasibility of a new scheme to reduce prices for large energy intensive business users. It also highlighted the importance of price transparency and easier switching for non-domestic customers.

stories.title: Fed has 'work to do' if above-target inflation remains
stories.summary: The US Federal Reserve will "have work to do" if policymakers are not confident that underlying inflation is returning to its 2% target, Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said today. His remarks acknowledged that financial conditions do not appear restrictive and marked the closest he has come to acknowledging interest rate hikes may be needed to ease price pressures. "Here is my standard - we must be confident that underlying inflation is moving to our objective, clearly and at sufficient speed. Otherwise, we have work to do. That's our job ... our mandate ... and our charge to keep," Warsh said in a remarks prepared for delivery to the Fed's Jackson Hole economic symposium in Wyoming. While much of the 16-page address focused on large issues, like the influence of artificial intelligence, that Warsh feels will be critical in the long run, it also included some key acknowledgements - including that "short-term interest rates are the predominant tool to achieve the dual mandate."

stories.title: US seeks to limit internships for international students
stories.summary: US President Donald Trump's administration has issued a memo for universities that ⁠seeks to restrict issuance of certain internship work authorisations for international students as the federal government warned that colleges not complying with the regulations may lose certification to enroll foreign students. The federal memo dated 24 August said the Student and Exchange Visitor Program, which is part of the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, has "observed a rise in Curricular Practical Training (CPT) authorisations that appear to violate regulatory requirements which permit CPT only where the training is an integral part of an established curriculum." "Failure to comply with SEVP regulations may result in an institution losing certification to enroll foreign students," the memo said. It resulted in some colleges, including the University of California, Los Angeles and the University of California, Berkeley, pausing certain applications ‌for work authorisations for international students.

stories.title: Ireland keeper Bazunu makes permanent move to Bolton
stories.summary: Republic of Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu has left Southampton and joined fellow Championship side Bolton Wanderers on a three-year deal. The move away from the Saints marks a fresh start for the 24-year-old. Although he made 19 appearances in the Championship last season, the Dubliner had fallen down the goalkeeping pecking order at St Mary's since signing for Southampton from Manchester City in 2022. In the second half of the 2025-26 campaign, the former Shamrock Rovers player spent an injury-affected spell on loan at Stoke City.

stories.title: Solan bound for Offaly, Hegarty remains as Wexford boss
stories.summary: Mike Solan is set to become the next manager of the Offaly footballers after being proposed by the Faithful County's management committee. Solan, who left his position as Longford boss earlier this month, will go forward for ratification at September’s county board meeting. If accepted, he will begin a three-year term and will be joined in the management team by former Mayo, Sligo and Longford coach Joe Keane and Offaly legend Nigel Dunne, who guided the Faithful minors to Leinster glory for the first time in 35 years in 2025. As well as Longford, Solan has previously managed the Mayo Under-21s and was part of Andy Moran’s management team in Leitrim.

stories.title: Bradley: Hard to qualify if you give up soft goals
stories.summary: Shamrock Rovers manager Stephen Bradley admitted his side were "disappointed" to exit Europe without reaching the league phase but disputed the claim that they had been offered an 'easier' qualifying path in 2026. A Graham Burke own goal with 16 minutes remaining against KuPS condemned Shamrock Rovers to European elimination and their fourth successive loss in Europe this season. It means that the Hoops have missed out on the lucrative league phase of the Conference League for the first time since the format was adopted. Drawing 1-1 from the first leg, Rovers had reached half-time with the game still goalless and had started the second half well, with Aaron Greene forcing a fine stop for KuPS goalkeeper Johannes Kreidl.

stories.title: Munster setback as Crowley ruled out until the new year
stories.summary: In what is a blow for Munster and Ireland ahead of the new season, out-half Jack Crowley is expected to be sidelined until early 2027 as he continues to recover from the effects of a lower limb vascular injury. The 26-year-old will also miss Ireland's Autumn Tests against Argentina, Fiji and South Africa, as well as any Nations Championship play-off games. After excelling for Ireland in the number 10 jersey during the Guinness Six Nations, Crowley was then absent for the closing stages of Munster's URC campaign and Ireland's opening games in the Nations Championship. Utmost in Munster's thinking is that the player is giving ample time to recover, with head coach Clayton McMillan saying: "Jack Crowley is a very important player for Munster and Ireland with a big future in the game and ensuring he gets back to 100% is the priority.

stories.summary: Freelance journalist and broadcaster, writing about music and the arts. stories.title: How can you spot a liar? An expert weighs in
stories.summary: With a new season of The Traitors Ireland this Sunday, 30 August, Dr Sabina Brennan, Psychologist & Neuroscientist, joined Drivetime to discuss why we lie and whether you can spot a liar. We've all heard you can spot a liar by their tells: scratching their nose, breaking eye contact, tripping over their words or changing their voice. In theory, we should be able to notice when they're being deceitful because they will start acting abnormally. But Brennan explains that these tells are mostly "myths". In reality, lying is a "natural ability", she says. "I think the important thing to remember about The Traitors is that it's a game, so it's not about people necessarily becoming dishonest. They've accepted a temporary role in which deception is permitted, and it's expected, and it's even rewarded.

stories.title: Over 2,400 missing after deadly Nepal, China floods
stories.summary: The number of people missing in Nepal and China leapt to more than 2,400 today, underscoring the scale of the disaster days after a tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept away villages and killed hundreds. Rescuers were battling through mud even as the threat of new floods loomed, with emergency teams recovering 584 bodies so far - and some of the dead swept downstream as far away as India. The new figures came as Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to a missing list already including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. Two Irish citizens, who have been named by the Nepalese Tourism Department as 46-year-old Santosh Sahu and 18-year-old Spandan Sahu, are among those missing.

stories.title: Mortgage approvals reached 15-year monthly high in July
stories.summary: Mortgage approvals reached their highest monthly levels in at least 15 years in July, latest figures from Banking & Payments Federation Ireland (BPFI) show. BPFI said first-time buyers (FTBs) continued to drive approvals, accounting for over half (3,575) of the 6,253 mortgages approved during the month. The total number of approvals was 14.4% higher than July 2025. Those remortgaging and switchers made up one fifth of all approvals - which was a 71.6% rise on last year.

stories.title: 7 ways to minimise dark circles at home
stories.summary: Dark circles are one of the most prolific skin concerns across all ages, and can be down to a myriad of reasons ranging from alcohol to hormones to lack of sleep or simply genetics. "Dark circles are slightly misleading because they are not really one condition," explains aesthetic practitioner Dr David Jack. "What we perceive as darkness underneath the eyes can come from increased melanin in the skin, visible blood vessels through very thin eyelid skin, changes in the underlying anatomy that create shadow or sometimes a mixture of all three." The colour can offer some indication of the cause. Jack says brownish circles are more suggestive of pigmentation, while blue, purple or reddish tones can indicate a greater vascular component.

stories.title: New levy for sustainable flood insurance fund proposed
stories.summary: Insurance Ireland is proposing a new levy of €24 per insured household to be placed into a "sustainable flood insurance fund" to address what it calls "Ireland's flood insurance protection gap". The levy is among a number of measures put forward in a report by the group representing insurers, which it said would allow homeowners to continue to access sustainable flood cover amid increased flooding risk due to climate change. It said the fund should be designed to ensure households in higher-risk areas can access flood insurance, where cover would otherwise be unavailable. Insurance Ireland said the Government could consider rebalancing existing insurance levies alongside the proposed new one that could allow its proposals to be introduced "with broadly no net additional cost to the average household".

stories.title: Foreign Affairs Dept spent almost €17,000 for Davos hotel
stories.summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs spent almost €17,000 on accommodation for the World Economic Forum (WEF) in Switzerland and nearly €15,000 on flights for a diplomat and family members posted overseas. The department also ran up an accommodation bill of just under €13,000 for hotel rooms during the COP30 climate conference in Brazil and paid over €7,000 for an 18-night stay at a swish New York hotel. The nightly cost of the room in New York was close to €400 for a staff member to stay at the four-star Shelburne Sonesta during the UN General Assembly. In total, the department spent almost €4.2m on flights last year with a further €2.58m paid for hotels and accommodation.

stories.summary: Sligo have reshuffled their managerial deck ahead of the 2027 season with last year's joint-managers Dessie Sloyan and Eamonn O'Hara pivoting into a manager-assistant manager arrangement. Sloyan will be the man in charge with Yeats County legend O'Hara becoming his assistant. The pair were joint-managers for just one season but the county have moved to make the adjustment ahead of the 2027 campaign. A statement from Sligo Co Board read: "At a meeting of its County Committee last evening (Monday, 24 August 2026) Sligo GAA endorsed the management teams for its senior football and hurling and U20 football teams for 2027.
